newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight rate steady on high liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight rate steady on high liquidity.

text.p: * Secondary trading in government securities moderate
Manila overnight money was wedged at an average of 10.5625 percent for the third straight session on Wednesday due to high liquidity, dealers said.
"Most of the big banks were square. Smaller banks borrowed early, pushing rates to a day's high of 10.875 percent," said one trader.
Rates softened towards the close due to the presence of a lot of lenders, they said.
Traders said banks invested their extra funds in the secondary market for short term government securities due to a dearth of investment alternatives.
Banks have been shying away from term reverse repos after these were slapped with a 20 percent tax.
"The Central Bank tried to entice us to invest in five-day reverse repos at 10.625 percent but there were no takers," said one trader.
Volume dropped to 18.424 billion pesos from 21.098 billion. Lenders swamped borrowers 30 to 18.
A Reuter survey of eight financial institutions showed three-month bills were bidded between 10.675 and 10.7 percent and offered at 10.575 to 10.65 percent.
Trading in six and 12-month bills was quiet, traders said.
Manila's overnight money market is expected to remain sideways for the rest of the week as high liquidity will persist, dealers said.
